links.targetTitle: The Resilience Technical Committee's eligibility bar demands
The Resilience Fund can be used when Sky itself is the targe

title: The Technical Committee's claim recommendation is declared both definitive and unappealable and non-binding
content:
Two consecutive provisions pull in opposite directions. A.2.9.1.1.1.4.2.2.5 gives the Resilience Technical Committee five working days to produce a payout recommendation and states that recommendations "are made in their sole and absolute discretion, are definitive, and are not subject to appeal." A.2.9.1.1.1.4.2.2.7 then states that "[t]he recommendations of the Resilience Technical Committee are non-binding and will not give rise to any right or claim to the beneficiaries nor give rise to any obligation or responsibility."

The combination is coherent only from one direction. A negative recommendation is definitive: the claimant cannot appeal it and the claim stops. A positive recommendation is non-binding: the Core Facilitator may still decline to trigger a Governance Poll (A.2.9.1.1.1.4.2.2.8), and SKY holders may still vote it down.

So the two clauses are not really contradictory — they are asymmetric. "Definitive" governs rejection, "non-binding" governs approval. The Committee is a veto gate, not a decision-maker.

The second clause's real work is liability shielding: the Committee members incur no "obligation or responsibility" for their recommendations. Read together with the requirement that they exercise "sole and absolute discretion," the design gives an unaccountable body unappealable negative power. That is defensible for a discretionary gift programme, but a beneficiary should not read "definitive" as any assurance that a favourable finding produces payment.
description: One provision makes the recommendation final with no appeal; the next makes it non-binding and productive of no right or obligation — so it can be neither challenged nor relied upon.
